items.q: What is The Constitution of God?
items.a: A fourteen-chapter theological manuscript by Mark H Steffen. It follows one argument from God's original constitution through sin, lineage, and restoration in Christ, and on to creation, the American constitutional ideal, and the purpose of life.
Fourteen chapters, in the 2026 author edition. The site groups them into three reading paths: foundations (chapters 1–5), restoration (chapters 6–10), and nation and purpose (chapters 11–14).

Individual readers, teachers and pastors, and study groups who want Scripture and the American experiment held in one constitutional frame. Media and institutions can use the Resources page and the contact form.

items.q: Where should a new reader start?
items.a: Take the reader quiz for a starting chapter, or open the chapter list and choose Foundations, Restoration, or Nation and Purpose. Readers who want the full argument should begin with chapter 1.

items.q: How do I request an interview or a speaking date?
items.a: Use the contact form and name the topic: media, event, rights, or a reader question.

items.q: Where can I buy the book?
items.a: The Constitution of God is available on Amazon. Signed sets and books for a study group can still be requested through the contact form.

cta.heading: Ready to Explore the Manuscript?
cta.body: Open the full chapter list, use the Resources page for context, or write in for media and speaking requests. Each major topic on this site has its own page.

items.title: The Original Constitution of God
items.summary: Explains how God established original principles to guide the creation of the spiritual and physical worlds. It explores the role of angels, free will, and God's intention to establish the Kingdom of Heaven on Earth.

items.title: The Constitutional Concept of God for the New World
items.summary: Discusses God's plan for human spiritual development and the selection of Adam and Eve to establish a heavenly world. It emphasizes spiritual perfection, free will, and humanity's responsibility to fulfill God's original purpose.

items.title: God's Original Constitution
items.summary: Explores God's original commandment to Adam and Eve to be fruitful, multiply, and have dominion over creation. It explains how Lucifer's jealousy and influence disrupted God's plan, leading to humanity's separation from Him.

items.title: The Origin of Sin
items.summary: Examines the spiritual and physical origins of sin through Lucifer's influence over Eve and Adam. The chapter describes how their disobedience introduced evil into human existence and prevented the establishment of God's intended heavenly kingdom.

items.title: Adam and Eve's Life After the Garden
items.summary: Describes Adam and Eve's struggles adjusting to physical life after leaving the Garden of Eden. It explores their children, particularly Cain and Abel, and how Satan's influence continued to affect subsequent generations.

items.title: Jesus as the Second Adam
items.summary: Explains Jesus' mission as the second Adam, sent to restore the original purpose that Adam and Eve failed to achieve. The chapter explores his lineage, relationship with John the Baptist, and how his crucifixion prevented the completion of that mission.

items.title: The Appearance of the Third Adam and Eve
items.summary: Discusses God's continued efforts to establish the Kingdom of Heaven following Jesus' death. It explains the need for a third Adam and Eve to restore the original heavenly family and complete the mission left unfinished by Jesus.

items.title: The Lineage Chain
items.summary: Explores the spiritual lineage connecting Adam and Eve to Jesus and the eventual appearance of the third Adam. It describes how the requirements for restoration developed over generations and why Korea became the chosen location for the next stage of God's plan.

items.title: The Birth of the Third Adam and the First Eve
items.summary: Explains the importance of establishing a spiritually pure man and woman who could fulfill God's original purpose. The chapter discusses Korea's selection, the restoration of the True Parents, and the distinction between paradise and the Kingdom of Heaven.

items.title: Jesus Must Return
items.summary: Examines Jesus' promise to return and complete his unfinished mission on Earth. The author identifies Reverend Sun Myung Moon as the third Adam, describing his spiritual encounter with Jesus and his responsibility to continue the work of restoration.

items.title: The Makeup of Creation
items.summary: Explores the spiritual structure of creation, the roles of God, angels, and humanity, and Satan's attempts to establish an opposing kingdom. It also discusses the author's belief that America and its national leaders have a special responsibility in preparing the world for God's Kingdom.

items.title: The American Constitution
items.summary: Draws parallels between God's original Constitution and the founding principles of the United States. It presents America's Declaration of Independence and Constitution as spiritually inspired foundations intended to support freedom and the establishment of God's Kingdom on Earth.

items.title: God's Desire
items.summary: Explains God's original vision of a harmonious universe where the spiritual and physical worlds exist in unity. It emphasizes absolute faith, love, and obedience as the guiding principles for humanity's spiritual growth and eternal relationship with God.

items.title: The Purpose of Life and the Desire of America
items.summary: Summarizes humanity's ultimate purpose as fulfilling God's Constitution through spiritual perfection, family, and responsible dominion over creation. It connects this mission to America's spiritual responsibility and the preparation needed to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

bio: Mark H Steffen writes at the meeting point of Scripture, constitutional language, and the practical question of purpose. The Constitution of God is his public argument: fourteen chapters that refuse to keep faith and citizenship in separate rooms.
He addresses readers who want more than devotion alone and more than politics alone — people who sense that Heaven's order and America's founding ideals were meant to be read together.
Speaking invitations, signed sets, and study-group orders are arranged through the contact page. The book itself is available on Amazon.
